Subject: Proposed DPA redline - data use & subprocessors

Hi Lauren,

Attached is Acme Cloud's proposed redline to the DPA. High level: they are asking us to narrow allowable data uses (no telemetry for product development unless explicitly anonymized), require 30-day notice for any new subprocessor and the right to audit subprocessors handling their data, and a shorter retention window for evaluation logs (45 days).

Can your team confirm whether these ask items are feasible for Redwood Dedicated/Private customers and whether we can provide the requested audit evidence? They flagged that this is a condition of final signature; procurement is ready to move quickly once legal and security align.

Attachment: ACME_DPA_Redline_v2.docx (docx, 68 KB)

Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed DPA redline - data use & subprocessors

Quick take from Product/Platform:
- Telemetry: our current quality telemetry for hosted models includes request/response hashes and some metadata (latency, model id, token counts). We do NOT persist full plaintext inputs by default for hosted customers, but for some legacy customers we have short-term enables for debugging. For Dedicated/Private (especially on-customer VPC), customer-controlled settings are common.

- Evaluation logs: a 45-day cap is feasible if we implement an automated TTL on the eval bucket and ensure any snapshots used for model tuning are purged. That work is ~2-3 engineer-days to lock down and test; acceptable for an enterprise onboarding sprint.

- Subprocessors: we publish a current list and can support 30-day notice. Audit rights are trickier — we can provide third-party audit reports (SOC2, ISO) and attestations, but on-site audits of our cloud vendors/providers may be limited. If Acme requires full vendor audit rights, we'll need legal to negotiate a tailored clause (maybe audit via summary reports or customer-provided auditors under NDA).

If security confirms acceptable evidence and legal shapes the language, we can meet most asks within the onboarding timeline.

—Vivek
VP Product, Redwood Inference
From: hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed DPA redline - data use & subprocessors

Thanks — adding Security perspective and an evidence checklist. Short answers:
1) Telemetry/data use: we need explicit language that any telemetry used for product development must be pseudonymized AND aggregated to a level where individual customer inputs cannot be reconstructed. Plaintext request/response must not be used for model training or analytics unless customer opt-in is explicit.

2) Retention: 45 days for evaluation logs is operationally reasonable, but we must ensure immutable backups or disaster recovery processes do not inadvertently keep copies longer; will require a short runbook change and S3 lifecycle policy enforcement.

3) Subprocessors + audit: we can provide current SOC2 and vendor attestations. On-site audits of our cloud providers (or their subs) are generally not permitted; recommend offering: (a) an annual summary audit package, (b) the ability for Acme to request additional evidence under NDA, and (c) a 30-day notice for new subprocessors with opt-out rights for materially new categories.

Attached: security_evidence_checklist.pdf (pdf, 22 KB) — includes SOC2 scope, KMS logs sample, encryption-at-rest summary and current subprocessor list.

Blockers: none immediate, but anything requiring plaintext retention for analytics is a no-go. If Product needs any non-anonymized telemetry for debugging, it must be scoped to a named support window with Acme consent.

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Director, Product Security

If Product can commit 3 business days to lock the TTL and Security can confirm the evidence package, I can push to get procurement to accept an amendment and keep the existing commercial terms.

Date: 2026-11-03T16:08:00Z
Subject: Redwood response & proposed edits — Acme DPA redline

Sarah / Acme team — thanks for the redline and for the patience while we coordinated internally. Below is a high-level summary of our position and next steps; attached is a tracked-change response for your review (Redwood_response_DPA_edits_20261102.docx).

Summary:
- Telemetry/data use: We cannot use unredacted customer request/response plaintext for model training or product analytics without explicit customer opt-in. For Acme we propose: any telemetry used for product improvement will be pseudonymized and aggregated; we will not use plaintext inputs for model training.
- Evaluation log retention: We agree to a 45-day retention period for evaluation logs; Redwood will implement TTLs and lifecycle policies and provide confirmation once configured.
- Subprocessors & audits: Redwood will provide an annual audit package (SOC2 report + vendor attestations) and will give 30 days' notice before adding new subprocessors. For additional evidence we can provide vendor reports and KMS logs under NDA; on-site audits of third-party cloud platforms are not feasible.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached tracked changes and let us know any narrow edits by EOD Friday (2026-11-06).
2) Security will deliver the evidence packet under NDA within 5 business days after countersignature.
3) Product will implement the eval-log TTL and send confirmation when complete (ETA 3 business days after countersign).

If this summary aligns, we can convert these edits into an amendment and route for signature. Grace — will coordinate the procurement timeline with Acme.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Enterprise Sales (Americas)
Redwood Inference
